action: Ban Palm Oil in products produced or sold in the UK
background: Palm Oil is found in many products you buy in the supermarket. It's also one of the main reasons for the destruction of rainforests, loss of wildlife habitat & climate change. Plenty of sustainable options are available and could be used instead. Encourage sustainability and ban palm oil in the UK.

action: To prevent all hydraulic fracturing from taking place within the Peak District.
background: In light to HM Government's recent decision to allow hydraulic fracturing via horizontal drilling, we state this decision should be repealed with an immediate effect. Not only due to the UK's recent agreement to tackle climate change in Paris, also preserve the Peak District for future generations.

action: Shift Agricultural Subsidies to Support Environmental Protections post-Brexit.
background: The government should redirect subsidies in a post-Brexit domestic agricultural policy, away from environmentally damaging farming, and towards environmental protections. Subsidies are needed to support farmers who tackle climate change, mitigate floods, increase biodiversity and soil health.
additional_details: The public are understandably discouraged with the current formulation of the Common Agricultural Policy. They don’t want to see their taxes being used to line the pockets of already wealthy landowners, or to prop up failing farming industries unconditionally. The public wants to see a domestic agricultural policy that is ahead of the curve by leading us on the path towards a low-carbon farming future, where our agricultural system provides significant benefits to the environment.

action: Restore the Department of Energy and Climate Change
background: With climate change being placed under the new 'Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy', it shows us that the PM does not take the issue seriously, although its effects are already showing. Protecting the planet is a huge job, that deserves it's own department.
additional_details: Numerous floods across the UK in such a short space of time, with three occurring in one month, show the disastrous effects of climate change on people and the environment. People could not leave their homes, homes and buildings were flooded out and many citizens suffered. Without proper care and protection, many more will follow.

action: Debate a vote of no confidence in Rt Hon Amber Rudd Sec of State (DECC)
background: The world needs a new agreement at the UN Climate Change Conference in Paris to de-carbonise and avoid excessive global warming. The Secretary of State for Energy & Climate Change is undermining renewable energy whilst promoting fossil fuels, the UK needs a credible voice at this vital conference.
additional_details: Actions contrary to combating climate change include: promoting fracking whilst overriding local democracy; removing renewable energy subsidies; plans to sell off the Green Investment Bank; giving up on zero carbon homes; weakening incentives to buy greener cars, putting community owned renewable energy schemes at severe risk, killing the green homes scheme and creating barriers to the conversion of fossil fuel power stations to biomass.

action: Stop all subsidies to the fossil fuel industry and subsidise renewables instead
background: It is now scientific consensus that not only is climate change the greatest threat facing our society but that the human activity of burning fossil fuels is the primary cause. The government is using public funds to supplement this industry that is destroying our children's future. You need to stop.
additional_details: Reported evidence of 6Bn in government subsidies -http://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/uk-government-pays-6bn-a-year-in-subsidies-to-fossil-fuel-industry-a6730946.html Scientific consensus - http://climate.nasa.gov/scientific-consensus David Cameron's sense of desperate urgency in his speech to the Paris Conference in 2015 - https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/pm-speech-to-the-cop21-summit-in-paris

action: Impose a Meat tax to help tackle one of the major causes of climate change.
background: Livestock create more greenhouse gases than all the world's vehicles combined. The world's current eating habits are not sustainable with our growing population. An additional tax on all meat products will encourage people to reduce their meat consumption and shift to more plant based products.
additional_details: Recent National Geographic article: http://www.nationalgeographic.com/foodfeatures/feeding-9-billion/?sa=X&ved=0CCgQ9QEwCGoVChMIm6Xu3J39xgIVAzkUCh1xfAKu Guardian article on cutting down meat consumption: http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2014/dec/03/eating-less-meat-curb-climate-change Nature Climate Change Journal: http://www.nature.com/nclimate/journal/v4/n1/full/nclimate2081.html Cowspiracy documentary: http://www.cowspiracy.com/

action: Ban supermarkets from packaging fruits and vegetables
background: Climate change is the single biggest threat to society. In addition, contamination by plastics has become a major issue with research saying that by 2050 there could be more plastics in the ocean than fish. A small, positive step would be to stop supermarkets from packaging fruits and vegetables.
additional_details: Such a ban would: - Reduce pollution (lower packaging production, less resources spent on recycling, reduced methane emissions from landfill sites) - Reduce strain on recycling facilities thus stop the export of waste (67% of British plastic waste is exported to the far east) - Increase consumer choice by avoiding bundling and decrease food waste (15m tonnes of food waste in the UK) - Lower prices of food - Contribute to a long-term vision of a zero waste society

action: Save Bolsover Community Hospital from closure
background: Bolsover community hospital is under threat from the public services cuts imposed by the current government. We need your help in saving our hospital which provides fantastic services and relieves the pressure on the larger hospitals which are already under strain.
additional_details: Bolsover community hospital is under threat of closure from the severe cuts facing all public services. The hospital offers physiotherapy treatment and advice, intermediate care services aiming to prevent people from being admitted to hospital which is essential for all major hospitals in the current financial climate and mental health services for the elderly which are essential in any community. Bolsover has lost a lot over the years, let's not add our hospital to the ever growing list.

action: Ban the spraying of any substance from aircraft over or near UK airspace.
background: Commercial aircraft are spraying substances unknown into our atmosphere during flight. Both UK registered and international carriers are seen spraying while in UK airspace. Commercial aircraft have been modified with aerosol delivery systems in the pylon for this purpose. The CAA are failing to act.
additional_details: I have collected evidence of: Aircraft producing clouds, which should not be the case. Aerosol delivery systems fitted to Airbus A320 family aircraft. Irregular flight patterns consistent with climate engineering programs. Chemicals being delivered to UK hub airports from Africa via scheduled flights. A refusal to act, acknowledge or investigate the issue from relevant organisations such as the CAA, NATS, MET Office.

action: The UK Government should retain our EU Renewable Energy targets as a minimum
background: There is speculation that the Government will drop EU Renewable Energy Targets if the UK leaves the EU. To address climate change & to ensure energy security we need a growing renewable energy sector for heat, power & transport fuels. The targets need to be retained with plans to achieve them

action: Stop scale down of Britains armed forces !
background: Proposal to scale down Britains armed forces specifically losing HMS Ocean and 42 Commando along with Main Battle Tanks . In current climate and with dwindling resources over last decade it is surely a rash perhaps foolish decision to keep cutting our nations defence !!
additional_details: Stop this policy of cutting back nations defence whilst purporting to be proud of the great Men and Women that serve .

action: Give all ancient woodland statutory legal protection
background: Ancient woodland is recognised as irreplaceable due to the specialised plant and animal species they support, not found elsewhere. As a result of habitat loss and fragmentation over the last 50 years 60% of those specialised species have declined significantly according to the State of Nature Report
additional_details: Ancient woodlands are a vital part of our cultural heritage, often containing archaeological remains waiting to be discovered, yet 85% of it has no legal protection. If we are to commit to our climate, flood alleviation and biodiversity action plan obligations these habitats must be protected from vandalism and development. At one time woodland covered the majority of the UK, as relics of this wild wood we must ensure that our ancient woodlands survive for the benefit of future generations.

action: Make the PassivHaus standard mandatory for new buildings in the UK
background: The PassivHaus standard delivers buildings that are healthy, comfortable, and cheap to heat, with heating bills and resulting carbon emissions less than 10% of the average UK building stock. Fuel poverty and climate change can be delivered through high levels of internal comfort.
additional_details: Despite the obvious benefits of the standard, the construction industry often requires more stick than carrot, with full take-up of the standard only happening in places where legislation has been brought about, such as Brussels, Frankfurt and Dún Laoghaire. While the Building Regs are based on the minimum acceptable standard the building industry will deliver buildings of low performance, with high energy wastage, poor comfort conditions and contradicting design and living practices.

action: Solar PV on all new buildings.
background: More than 3,000,000 people worldwide have died from climate change, not to mention the damage to other species. It's possible to provide the UK's electrical needs with rooftop Solar PV & storage. Forcing developers to install at new build will be a big step to reducing CO2e emissions.
additional_details: World Health Organisation website states that 150,000 people a year were dying from climate change related issues in 2000 and this will increase to 250,000 people a year by 2030. http://www.who.int/mediacentre/factsheets/fs266/en/ Cornwall Solar Panels website shows how much Solar PV is needed to power the UK. http://www.cornwallsolarpanels.co.uk/news/power-to-the-people-the-no-bills-uk-energy-revolution/

action: Introduce meat and dairy taxes to correct market failure in the food industry
background: Food production causes a quarter of all greenhouse gas emissions that are driving global warming. Both the UN International Research Panel and the Oxford University Martin Programme have suggested pricing in the environmental impacts of meat and dairy are vital steps to combating climate change.
additional_details: The Oxford report states average surcharges of 40% on beef and 20% on milk would account for the damage they cause people via climate change and Maarten Hajer, the lead author of the UN report has recommended similar action. We hereby call on the government to implement such taxes to help meet our international obligations to combat climate change. http://www.nature.com/nclimate/journal/vaop/ncurrent/pdf/nclimate3155.pdf https://www.dropbox.com/sh/bhhivquadq7ycnd/AAAIl8mVW9GCiOyGwk71At_ra?dl=0

action: Put climate change at the top of the agenda in discussions with President Trump.
background: At this crucial time of establishing relationships with the new President, it should be made clear that climate change is the most pressing concern we currently have.

action: The UK must ratify the Paris Agreement on climate change immediately
background: At COP21 in December of 2015 real progress was made in creating global agreement for a low carbon future. For these agreements to be legally binding 55 countries representing 55% of global emissions must ratify the Paris Agreement. The US and China have just ratified- the UK must follow suit.
additional_details: The UK represents 1,55% of global emissions, so its signature would make a tangible difference http://unfccc.int/paris_agreement/items/9444.php http://climateanalytics.org/hot-topics/ratification-tracker.html We stand a real chance for progress now China and the US have signed (the worlds two biggest emitters by far). http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-37265541

action: Introduce Ombudsman for Future Generations & UN Sustainable Development Goals
background: The UK government agreed to 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals, including: environmental protection, reducing emissions, clean energy, responsible consumption & production. An Ombudsman to protect the future of humanity against climate change is needed. As is clear policy to enable accountability.
additional_details: The government must act fast to provide baseline statistics. There must be procedure in place so that those acting against climate change for future generations can be made accountable. An action plan and policy must be clear and transparent. Management of SDGs and climate action must not come under the umbrella of Dept. Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy, it requires its own leader and must be woven into all other departments as it affects all other departments.

action: Improve air quality & tackle climate change by promoting shale gas & renewables
background: Around 30% of UK electricity is still generated by burning coal, releasing large quantities of climate changing CO2 emissions and air pollutants. Government can change this by promoting a shale gas and renewables boom, avoiding 'technology tribalism' and helping secure our clean energy future.
additional_details: Coal-fired power generation in the United States has fallen to its lowest level since 1949 as a result of a shale gas and renewables boom. It's helped to reduce climate changing CO2 emissions by a massive 32% The UK Government can create the conditions for us to repeat this success by designating wind, solar, shale gas, biogas and waste-to-energy as Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects, helping to cut planning red-tape, improve investor certainty and get more capacity built.

action: Co-ordinate an international intervention on Trump's US climate policy
background: The Trump administration intends to revive a fossil-fuel economy and withdraw from the Paris Agreement. If US climate policy undermines global climate change targets, the UK government should intervene on behalf of the UK population and co-ordinate the intervention of other nations as well.

action: Put tackling climate change at the top of the government's agenda.
background: For too long climate change has been a secondary consideration, yet it is the defining challenge of our time. I call on the government to create a separate department and minister of state for climate change, and to make climate change a central consideration of all future policy-making decisions.
additional_details: We must rapidly increase investment in research and technologies to understand climate science, realise new technologies, quickly decarbonise our economy and increase our resillience to future uncertainty. This can wait no longer. We need strong leadership from this government. Even the possibility of accelerating climate change should shock us out of complacency. http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/climate-change-game-over-global-warming-climate-sensitivity-seven-degrees-a7407881.html

action: Re thinking the budget for Essex Police to save PCSO s jobs
background: Essex police are having to restructure front line policing due to the amount of money they receive from government. Essex is a major county with big links and easy access to London. Losing PCSO'S from the front line due to budget constraints in the current climate is wrong. Help increase budget

action: Put restrictions on the amount of packaging used by British supermarkets.
background: In the light of the varied problems of climate change and waste disposal, it is inexcusable that supermarkets produce vast quantities of unnecessary packaging. Consumables, such as fruit and vegetables, confectionery and ready meals, do not need to be enclosed in multiple layers of plastic.
additional_details: Estimates put our annual levels of waste from packaging at around 5 mega-tonnes, this constitutes between a quarter and a third of our domestic waste. Responsibility for disposal and recycling of over-packaging should not be put on the consumer. Packaging to enclose goods such as bananas or tomatoes is entirely avoidable whilst for other products, such as confectionery, multiple layers of packaging are often used where one would suffice.

action: Swansea Bay Tidal Lagoon project needs full Government commitment
background: This would be an iconic project, a world first. It would make the UK a world leader in tidal energy. David Cameron has recently said that his enthusiasm for the project has 'reduced.' The Cameron Government have already undermined wind and solar power. Let's make sure they don't destroy tidal power.
additional_details: Project website: http://www.tidallagoonswanseabay.com/ Climate change science: http://www.skepticalscience.com/

action: Accelerate the pace of greenhouse gas emissions reductions in the UK
background: To support the Paris agreement on climate change, the UK must: enact immediate measures to eliminate fossil fuel subsidies; increase public & private investment in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and low carbon technologies; decarbonise the transport system; and promote sustainable consumption.
additional_details: With the historic international agreement on climate change reached at COP21 in Paris, the UK has committed to "global peaking of greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible", with "developed countries taking the lead". However, the Committee on Climate Change has stated that "action is needed in this Parliament to ensure the pace of emissions reduction accelerates". Clearly there is a now a gap between our international obligations and domestic action, and this needs to be urgently addressed.

action: End all government subsides and other financial aid to the fossil fuel industry.
background: The UK government provides the domestic fossil fuel industry with funds to the tune of £6 billion annually. This industry, endangering all of us by intensifying climate change, is getting money from our government at the expense of the taxpayer. This has to stop before it is too late.
additional_details: Direct subsides are hard to calculate – Reasonable mid-range figure is £6 billion annually, given by widely trusted sources such as the Independent and the Overseas Development Institute(ODI) however the UK claims not to have any using an irrational definition. The International Monetary Fund puts the figure much higher at £26b. This petition's specific demand is that fossil fuel subsides, as defined by the ODI are to be abolished by 2020 and the extra revenue should be invested in clean energy.

action: Debate the implementation of a carbon tax in the House of Commons
background: Climate change is currently happening and economic experts cite a carbon tax as a solid and progressive step. Reducing carbon consumption and also taxation needed from other sources. Carbon tax would drastically reduce the rates of income tax. More money for you and a better environment.
additional_details: https://www.carbontax.org/why-a-carbon-tax/ 'A robust tax on carbon pollution will create powerful incentives inducing policy-makers and individuals to reduce carbon emissions through conservation, substitution and innovation' 'Currently, the prices of electricity, gasoline and other fuels reflect little or none of the long-term costs from climate change or even the near-term health costs of burning fossil fuels'

action: Ensure plastic food packaging, plates and cutlery are environmentally friendly.
background: France has passed a new law to ensure all plastic cups, cutlery and plates are compostable and made of biologically-sourced materials. The UK should be making plans to implement similar plastics and packaging controls in order to tackle the growing problems of pollution and climate change.
additional_details: By 2050 there will be more plastic in our oceans than fish (World Economic Forum). Nearly a third of all plastics leak into the environment where they end up eaten by wildlife or in floating rubbish dumps in the sea. The British government needs to take some kind of definitive action against the use of plastics in our country, if we’re going to have any chance of mitigating the problem of waste in a growing global population.

action: Give free public transport to homeless people in UK
background: Whilst we find ways and seek solutions to Homelessness it would be a good start by offering access to public transport. This way we would offer them some respite and support that they need in order to improve their lives. Moreover, it would not cost us much as it is already there.
additional_details: In the current climate Homelessness is rising and there are no easy solutions to this. Local Authorities are struggling to cope with the demand and are not able to house most people registered as Homeless due to the lack of Housing supply. We believe that it would be only just fair that as a great country, United Kingdom would allow anyone who is registered as Homeless to have free public transport. This would enable them to go to work, attend job centres, hospital or housing appointments.

action: Involve the British public in the fight against climate change
background: Our collective CO2 emissions are just those of each individual added together: each of us can and must limit our carbon footprint. As well as strong legislative action, the government should contact every home to explain the reality and danger of climate change and advise what each of us should do.
additional_details: The WHO: "Climate change is among the greatest health risks of the 21st century." Personal actions should be prioritised by relative impact. Former DECC Chief Scientific Advisor Sir David MacKay urged these steps, among others: Stop (or dramatically reduce) flying Replace driving with public transport, cycling or walking Reduce the energy needed to make products we buy (frequent new electronics & clothing, packaging) Eat vegetarian 6/7 days Turn heating to 15-17 degrees Increase home insulation.

action: Impose economic sanctions on the USA if they renege on the Paris Climate deal
background: Climate change is an immediate threat to global ecosystems, livelihoods and communities. The Paris climate agreement is international law and must be fulfilled in order to mitigate dangerous warming. We call for economic sanctions on the USA if they withdraw from the agreement.
additional_details: Climate change will rapidly escalate within decades unless urgent action is taken. The USA contribute 16% of global CO2 emissions and must play a leading role in fulfilling the Paris agreement. If the USA withdraw this could lead to catastrophic consequences, with the poorest people in the world suffering the most. If they withdraw, the UK should impose economic sanctions on the USA and encourage its allies to do likewise. www.newscientist.com/article/2112164-president-trump-means-we-cant-escape-a-dangerously-warmer-world/ www.scientificamerican.com/article/trump-picks-top-climate-skeptic-to-lead-epa-transition www.independent.co.uk/news/science/climate-change-game-over-global-warming-climate-sensitivity-seven-degrees-a7407881.html

action: Technical and financial support to fossil fuel and steel industry for survival.
background: Coal fired power stations and steel industry are facing an uncertain future due to environmental policy changes implemented by UK and EU government. Need a taskforce under UK govt. to monitor these industrial sector and declare a financial and technical support package to protect and reform them.
additional_details: Ferrybridge and Eggbrough power stations announced plant closure recently. TATA Steel closed its Scunthorpe plant partially and made more than one thousand workers redundant across UK. Many coal mines closed and workers lost jobs. UK government should support these industries financially and technically to reform to suit present climate change regulations. Also need a plan to protect the workforce through retraining and rehabilitate them in future redundancies or closures arise.

action: Start a Government funded Keep Britain Tidy Campaign on TV and in the Newspapers
background: I have been picking up litter in my community for over three years and have filled 600 carry bags. I am ill health retired and find it difficult bending some days. The amount of litter on our streets is appalling and in the countryside. I have been on TV local news
additional_details: Search You tube "ITN NEWS REPORT ON LITTER IN CRAWLEY" this will highlight my campaign nicely. Crawley Observer, Yorkshire post, Crawley News and a few more as well. I walk my dog daily picking up the same type of litter day in day out. Same route its dropped over and over sometimes a few feet from a bin. We need to educate the young through a vigorous campaign. We need to make fast food chains advertise too within there adverts on TV and in the Paper. Climate change is partly the result of littering our planet.

action: Stop plans to pay for the restoration of properties belonging to the super rich.
background: In the current economic climate, it is morally wrong to use public funds to pay for the restoration of such buildings as Wentworth Woodhouse and Buckingham Palace. The owners of said properties should be the ones to pay and the money earmarked for this should be passed on to the NHS immediately.

action: The UK government should not enter into any trade negotiations with the USA.
background: The US administration has put forward the climate change denying America First Energy Policy. Until such time as this policy is reversed and they take clear and measurable steps to reduce C02 emissions the UK must not enter into any trade negotiations with the USA.
additional_details: https://www.whitehouse.gov/america-first-energy

action: Government should stage a new cultural Festival of Britain
background: The Opening Ceremonies of the 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games did much to tell the world what makes Britain Great. Let's have a cultural Festival of Britain in this post Brexit climate to demonstrate what an amazing nation this is and that we continue to welcome the world
additional_details: Let's celebrate what makes this nation great in the ways that we did over 2012. Let's reach out and show the world what a vibrant and amazing country we live in, what we have to give to the world through culture and the wider creative sectors which lie at the heart of our thriving knowledge economy

action: Introduce a nationwide carbon tax applying to both citizens and corporations.
background: This petition is a call for politicians to take action against the threat of climate change before it is too late. We are calling for nationwide taxation on all activities and products contributing to the emission of carbon dioxide, which would set our country on the path to a sustainable future.

action: Make the environment and climate change issues far more important in UK politics
background: The way the environment and climate change issues are treated by politics is disgraceful. All parties seem to shun them in favour of more "prominent" matters. But humans are destroying the planet. We need to, and politics needs to, move the environment to the front of the agenda. We need to save it.

action: Vehicles powered by fossil fuels should be banned from UK cities by 2025
background: Air pollution is linked to 40,000 early deaths per year in the UK. A major contributor to the state of air quality is the use of vehicles powered by fossil fuels on Britain's roads. Climate change and health implications aside, just imagine the air in our cities being as fresh as an alpine breeze.
additional_details: Clean air technology exists in the form of electric engines, batteries, and hydrogen fuel cells. Cars and other vehicles powered by this technology are currently expensive, and out of the reach of most consumers and business. However, legislation could increase the pace of innovation within automotive industries in order to make such technology cheap and available to all. This will be a big step towards the cleaner brighter future that we all deserve.

action: Set a legal target for the power sector to decarbonise by 2030.
background: A decarbonisation target will virtually eliminate greenhouse gas emissions in electricity. It will ensure that the UK meets its climate targets and presents strong commitment against climate change to other countries, as well as ensuring the government cannot backtrack on climate change mitigation.
additional_details: The government's own advisors on climate change, the Committee on Climate Change, recommends reducing emissions from power to below 100g CO2/kWh (compared to 450g in 2014) to decarbonise the power sector. Energy investor clarity is also needed for new technologies to develop, and with this development is also the opportunity for new jobs and economic growth. These new technologies are either soon cost competitive with conventional sources or will be by 2030 (such as offshore wind by 2025).

action: Reinstate the 2006 plan for all new homes built after 2016 to be zero carbon.
background: The plan would have ensured that all new dwellings from 2016 would generate as much energy on-site – via renewable sources, e.g. wind or solar energy – as they would use in heating, hot water, lighting and ventilation. This would be alongside tighter energy efficiency standards.
additional_details: Zero Carbon homes are not more expensive - designers at Cardiff University built a zero carbon house at no extra cost here: (http://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-33544831). Also, they will be cheaper to run as energy costs could be zero or even negative, therefore earning the owners money. As well as the economic benefits of zero carbon homes, reducing carbon emissions is also important for climate change; and reducing energy dependency on other countries (i.e. by importing gas and oil)

action: Introduce a penny tax on plastic bottles
background: Plastic bottles our damaging out health. There are toxic chemicals in plastic bottles, including polycarbonates which are linked to conditions such as cancer and an increased risk of diabetes. Many bottles are also then polluted and ultimately damage animals and contribute to climate change.
additional_details: There are now areas of sea across the world almost entirely covered in plastics, so often the result of thoughtless pollution of materials we consume readily every day - such as plastic bottles. This pollution has done great damage to the nature and sea and wildlife in areas where currents have taken these polluted materials. A charge would go some way to encouraging less pollution and as a result, less damage to our planet's natural environments and wildlife. It is also the case that many of the chemicals contained in plastic bottles are detrimental to both human and animal health; yet we consume these goods unknowingly and without due thought.

action: Make Climate Change education a compulsory aspect of the UK national curriculum.
background: Climate change is arguably the most complex problem ever faced by humanity and the consequences of inaction will be most felt by our children. The fact that this information is not delivered in our schools with urgency is unacceptable and we are letting all future generations down!
additional_details: How can we expect to encourage global collaboration and eco-innovation in the UK's future if our children are not even aware of this serious problem? Human induced climate change cannot be ignored any more. We are letting our children/country/planet down by not encouraging active debate on this issue in our schools. Current curricula: https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/national-curriculum. IPCC Climate Report: http://ipccwg2.gov/AR5/images/uploads/WG2AR5_SPM_FINAL.pdf

action: Review and reconsider the social work profession and forthcoming reforms.
background: The Government has announced a swathe of reforms for the Social work profession that seems to focus on accreditation and more justification processes for practitioners.
additional_details: The pressures of front line staff juggling high increasingly complex caseloads in a climate of high poverty, low investment and social challenge has been unaddressed again.the high demand created by endless administration and paperwork ignored, the hours of expected unpaid overtime and burnout unconsidered. I want this issue re-debated and recognition that the challenges social work faces aren't down to a lack of commitment, qualification or professionalism. Social workers know what needs to change to deliver better outcomes for vulnerable children and adults. Why has the government not asked us?

action: Remove all subsidies for fossil fuels, use them to subsidise renewable energy.
background: It's impossible for the government to simultaneously state their commitment to combating climate change and subsidise fossil fuels to the extent that they do. The amount of money spent on renewable energy is meanwhile decreasing. Spending more on renewable's is the only way to show real commitment.
additional_details: Subsidies for fossil fuels which approach £6 billion a year are being given to companies which generate profits in the hundreds of millions. That money is far better used to subsidies to production and implementation of renewable energies or to subsidies the household energy bills. There is an estimated 26.7 million households in the UK, the money could be used to decrease the annual energy bill by £224. Stop giving to the rich, start giving to the people.

action: Introduce a revenue-neutral carbon tax
background: In order to minimise further climate change, we need to move away from the use of fossil fuels that pollute our atmosphere and oceans with carbon. This can be achieved by introducing a tax on carbon producing activities, while lowering tax elsewhere to mitigate the overall cost to the public.
additional_details: Since the industrial revolution, we have been releasing vast amounts of carbon into the atmosphere and oceans. If we continue adding to the natural carbon cycle as we are today, climate change and rising sea levels will result in the loss of coastal cities which are home to the majority of people on Earth. The only way to stop this is to move away from carbon polluters, which requires disincentivising carbon polluting activity, while incentivising sustainable alternatives. Please support this.

action: Start an immediate program of flood resilient bridge and infrastructure building
background: Many bridges in flooded areas are now unsafe and unfit for purpose. Given the changes in climate and traffic density we call upon the government to institute an immediate program of public works, to restore and replace outdated bridges with modern single span bridges and infrastucture.
additional_details: Bridge collapses and closures across the UK demonstrate the need for bridges built to modern standards and with modern materials that will be resilient against modern weather conditions. Local communities cannot afford this and need central government to take urgent and immediate action for the sake of communities and business.

action: Hold a referendum on 'What is the ideal population level of the UK to aim for?'
background: The hotly debated 'immigration question' is a small part of a much bigger picture. The world is overpopulated and this is one of the root causes of climate change, water and food scarcity, and the mass extinction of species. The UK must decide democratically how to respond to this global problem.

action: Take more action to reduce activities that contribute to global climate change.
background: Deployment of mitigation technologies, as well as deployment of non fossil fuel energy sources will be necessary to achieve a stabilization of the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Support renewables, divest from fossil fuels, tackle pollution and stop Fracking.
additional_details: http://www.greenfacts.org/en/climate-change-ar4/ http://www.greenfacts.org/en/climate-change-ar5-science-basis/index.htm One Million Climate Jobs: Tackling the Environmental and Economic Crisis http://www.campaigncc.org/climatejobs

action: Let there be a parliamentary debate on fracking under protected national parks
background: The gov has used “a parliamentary backdoor to put through these weak regulations without a proper debate”1. Amber Rudd pledged an "outright ban on fracking in national parks [and] sites of special scientific interest”2. Drilling on/under these sites will pollute the area. Stop cuts to renewables.
additional_details: 1. Lisa Nandy, Labour's shadow energy and climate secretary. http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-britain-shale-policy-idUKKBN0TZ28420151216 2. Amber Rudd, the then parliamentary undersecretary of state for climate change. http://www.publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm201415/cmhansrd/cm150126/debtext/150126-0002.htm She also said: The regulations... recognise areas that should be given a high level of protection, even if the development is outside the site boundary.

action: Fully fund feed in tariffs and reverse planned cuts to feed in tariffs.
background: This is important to support the renewable energy sector and to safe guard jobs, particularly in the solar energy sector.

Our present Parliamentry system is evidentially no longer fit for purpose. Increasing numbers of Peers and their unaccountability surely is not sustainable in a modern democracy.

action: Debate in Parliament how the UK can get to net zero carbon emissions
background: On April 13th 2017, the New Zealand Parliament debated how they can transition to net zero carbon emissions. The UK Parliament should do the same. Halting climate change is perhaps the number one issue facing humanity, has cross-party support, but is not given the time in Parliament it deserves.

action: A second referendum should be held to determine whether the UK leaves the EU.
background: Politicians are fearful of going against the wishes of the people, so lets put this back to the people who now have much more qualified information with which to make a qualified decision. A second referendum should be held before invoking Article 50.
additional_details: It appears to be relatively clear and agreed that the persuasive arguments used to support the Brexit stance were vague suppositions at the best and barefaced lies at the worst. We are now also in a very different political climate following the election of Donald Trump. It should now be time for the Citizens of the UK to participate in their own 'reality check' before we push this Country into an irreversible situation.

action: Theresa May should ensure the UK ratifies the Paris Accord on climate change
background: This climate deal may be the last chance the international community has to help prevent runaway climate change by limiting carbon emissions and putting sustainability at the forefront of economic decision making.

action: Make country good by making PM listen
background: We think the country is doing bad and want it to not do bad. The PM can make the country better and not rubbish. We have ideas of what to do. Please help us youths of whom want a gooder countrie for us to live in
additional_details: What to do: Abolish university fees Raise the tax for the rich Lower the tax for the poor Tax on Queen's money More money to education More money to NHS More money to prison system More money to climate change prevention schemes Take money out of coal and oil schemes More money to foreign aid More money to justice system - reform not deterrence Money to libraries and museums Make marijuana legal and tax it Raise consumption and environmental Raise corporation tax Lower inheritance tax

action: Parliament must ratify the Paris Climate Agreement before the PM leaves office.
background: Climate change continues. Immediate measures must be taken to reduce our global carbon footprint. Ratification of this agreement will demonstrate to the UK people and the world, that this Government understands the severity of the issue, and is serious about inter-generational climate justice.
additional_details: http://unfccc.int/paris_agreement/items/9444.php U N Framework Convention on Climate Change Paris Agreement – Status of Ratification "Authoritative information on the status of the Paris Agreement, including information on signatories to the Agreement, ratification and entry into force, is provided by the Depositary, through the United Nations Treaty Collection website, and can be accessed here- https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetails.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XXVII-7-d&chapter=27&lang=en

action: Halt the triggering of Article 50, in the light of presidential election result.
background: The massive geopolitical change resulting from the US presidential election so increases the risk and uncertainty surrounding the proposed withdrawal of the UK from the EU, that it is prudent to call a halt to the triggering of Article 50, to have time to consider all the implications for the UK.
additional_details: There has been a very significant change since the referendum, with political and economic ramifications that require due consideration. There is no urgent need for Article 50 to be invoked. In the light of recent events, current haste would appear ill-judged. It is sensible in the current climate to adopt caution - the UK risks alienating itself from its European allies, when the need for togetherness may be at its greatest. More deliberation will produce a better decision for the UK.

action: Stand up against climate change. Stop Donald Trump's censorship of science.
background: The UK Government to pressurise Trump and his administration to protect the integrity of accepted scientific evidence. To pressurise them to uphold their commitments to the Paris Agreement 2015 and other environmental legislation.

action: Delay triggering of Article 50 for at least one year from next General Election
background: The two major political parties in the UK are currently in turmoil. The PM and a number of shadow cabinet ministers have resigned. The climate of political uncertainty means now is not the right time to leave the EU: we should wait until we have new team of leaders who have settled into their roles.
additional_details: Whilst it is undeniable that 52% of the country are currently unhappy with their lives and wish to see change, there will be enough change in the coming months without adding to the political instability by triggering Article 50. Whether or not there is a second referendum, we believe that any new Prime Minister should not implement Article 50 until his or her team have settled into their roles and a clear plan and risk assessment for leaving the EU is laid out before the public.

action: Allow Nicola Sturgeon to run for Prime Minister after Cameron's resignation.
background: Following the incredibly tight EU Referendum result, the most qualified and experienced leader to lead us through the difficult times to come - David Cameron - was forced to anounce his resignation due to a fundamental disagreement with the apparent will of the British people.
additional_details: Now that the position is due to be vacant at an earlier point than anticipated, the selection of possible candidates for the role are, in the eyes of many British people, unsuitable in the current climate. Therefore it is only logical to draw on the resource that is Nicola Sturgeon in our time of need: somebody who is already experienced in running a country and whose position in power will allow the Scottish people to feel less marginalised and act as a much needed cohesive force within the UK.

action: End Transmission Of Cruel Acts Towards Live Animals For Entertainment Purposes
background: We believe that inflicting harm to animals of any kind, such as eating them live or dropping them from height, for entertainment purposes is perverse and should not be encouraged. We demand that shows such as 'I'm a Celebrity' should not be allowed to broadcast such actions on UK TV.
additional_details: Examples of Animal Cruelty broadcast on I'm A Celebrity. -Eating live animals such as spiders, worms, leeches -Dropping animals from dangerous heights causing injury and death. -Placing them in tanks with people, causing distress upon the animal -Introducing them to uninhabitable climates, therefore the animal becoming unwell due to an unnatural environment.

action: REGULATE PALM OIL AND ITS USE TO BE CLEARLY LABELLED ON FRONT OF PRODUCTS.
background: Manufactures using palm oil in everyday products is contributing to deforestation. It is an abuse of power & influence, as many consumers lack information, opportunity and means to make a palm oil free choice. For others not choosing palm oil is unreasonably difficult and time consuming.
additional_details: The time consuming often untenable hunt through ingredients is unacceptable and customers should be facilitated to make ethical shopping choices as easily as possible, especially on issues that may affect climate change and the destruction of the world’s rainforest. The use of palm oil shoud be regulated to curb its use and clear proactive labelling on the front of products to encourage and facilitate palm oil free shopping as well as to encourage manufactures to make alternatives available.

action: How child maintenance is worked out
background: In the current climate, is it fair to disregard hundreds of pounds paid each month in child support and allow the claimants to receive full benefit entitlement paid from tax payers money , often making tax payers worse off

action: Restore the Department for Energy and Climate Change
background: This petition calls on the Prime Minister and her government to reverse the decision to abolish the Department for Energy and Climate Change.
additional_details: A Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs is simply not good enough. Climate change is a serious issue that will have a lasting impact on future generations. It should hold an important place at the heart of government.

action: To reinstate the Department of Energy and Climate Change
background: The Department of Energy and Climate Change has recently been killed off by Theresa May. Climate change is one of the biggest challenge we face and must be taken seriously. We need this department to continue making our country as energy efficient and renewable as possible.

action: Introduce a Carbon Tax to combat climate change
background: Climate change is the most important issue our society is faced with. Introducing a carbon tax into the UK would help us as a nation minimize our carbon tax and set an example to the rest of the world. One option would be to reduce income tax at the same time as introducing a carbon tax.
additional_details: This may be our last chance to stop climate change. If the average temperature rises by 2°C then coral reefs will die. Not only are these natural phenomenons beautiful and unique, coral reef plants and the animals that inhabit them are important sources of new medicines that are being developed to treat cancer, arthritis, Alzheimer's disease, heart disease, and other diseases due to their amazing biochemistry. Also, if the Greenland ice cap melts completely, as it is already starting too, then the fresh water might completely stop the Gulf Stream, which is a natural ocean current that keeps us warm. If the Gulf Stream stops then precipitation will fall as snow instead of rain, and over time could lead to the UK's climate becoming more like that of eastern Russia during winter.

action: Take a strong stance against the USA if it goes back on climate change promises.
background: The Republican Party does not accept climate science and opposes regulating climate pollution. The Republican Party will control all the law making bodies in the USA and may repeal climate change laws. Such action is unacceptable & the UK must take the strongest possible stance to stop it.

action: Strictly ban the construction of houses near rivers in London and elsewhere
background: Should the government promise better and faster flood responses, it must stop people from building houses near rivers and ensure well funded and organised flood defences installed in critical areas.
additional_details: Flooding is the greatest risk for riverfront property owners. Even with elaborate flood control systems in place, varying water levels throughout the year can cause trouble for homes that are too low and too close to the banks. The risk of flooding increases significantly with rivers that have little or no flood control. The fallout from flooding could lead to extensive property damage and expensive, time-consuming repairs. So based on current predictions of climate change, it's a must-to-do.

action: We call for a cross party environmental inquiry and environmental audit.
background: We are calling for a cross party environmental inquiry and environmental audit into the short, medium and long term consequences for the United Kingdom. This should involve proper scientific advice and extend into universities to find the right experts in the various fields required to perform this
additional_details: It is clear to most informed people that a looming environmental disaster is very likely to occur if nothing is done to prevent it. Greenland glaciers started melting 2 months early this year, the beginning of a chain reaction that will result in the desalination and slowing of the ocean conveyor. The UK will experience temperatures similar to Canada and ultimately to the death and sulphurfization of the worlds oceans. We should have been a World leader in Climate Change !"

action: Ban supermarkets from packaging fruits and vegetables
background: Climate change is the single biggest threat to society. In addition, contamination by plastics has become a major issue with research saying that by 2050 there could be more plastics in the ocean than fish. A small, positive step would be to stop supermarkets from packaging fruits and vegetables.
additional_details: Such a ban would: - Reduce pollution (lower packaging production, less resources spent on recycling, reduced methane emissions from landfill sites) - Reduce strain on recycling facilities thus stop the export of waste (67% of British plastic waste is exported to the far east) - Increase consumer choice by avoiding bundling and decrease food waste (15m tonnes in the UK) - Lower prices of food - Contribute to a long-term vision of a zero waste society

action: If Trump is making a state visit don't use the tax payers money to fund it
background: If Donald Trump is to make a state visit to the UK, do not fund it by the taxpayer's money. Millions of people have made it very clear that they are outraged by Trump and his racism and bigotry, it is more than unfair to fund his visit by the people's money.
additional_details: It will cost £10 million of tax payer's money to fund a state visit, the money could be spent on the nhs, education or many other useful essentials that are struggling in the current climate.

action: Ask Prime Minister May to pardon all black families DNA criminalised in UK.
background: It has effectively criminalised Britain’s black communities on an unprecedented scale, creating a climate of distrust in both law enforcement and crime prevention agencies among minority ethnic communities.
additional_details: The numbers of innocent people from Britain’s black communities profiled on this database far outstrips that of any other group living in the UK. DNA profiles can be used to track an individual or their relatives, and the samples contain unlimited genetic information. This has driven poverty high and increased unsocial behaviors, crime and the culture of street offenses, we belief that its a carefully concealed plan profiling an ethnic group of people which leads to cleansing.
